hints: Notice the axes are $e$ vertical against $F$ horizontal, with P marking the elastic limit, so only the curve beyond P is plastic.
Recall work done stretching is $dW = F \, de$, so on this plot it is the area counted in horizontal strips against the $e$-axis, not the area under the curve.
Compare total area to the $e$-axis with the part up to extension at P to isolate the extra strip between the $e_P$ level and the final extension.
walkthrough: Identify the axes: extension $e$ is plotted vertically and force $F$ horizontally, and point P is the elastic limit, so deformation beyond P is plastic.
State the rule for work: a small extension $de$ needs work $dW = F \, de$, so total work is $W = \int F \, de$.
On an $e$ against $F$ graph this integral is the area between the curve and the $e$-axis, built from horizontal strips of width $F$ and height $de$.
Split that area at P: the area from $0$ to $e_P$ beside the straight section is elastic work, and the area from $e_P$ to the final $e$ beside the curved section beyond P is plastic work.
That plastic strip is bounded below by the horizontal line through P, above by the final extension, on the left by the $e$-axis and on the right by the curve. This is option C.

A.explanation: This is the area between the curve and the $F$-axis, $\int e \, dF$, which does not equal work done.

B.explanation: This is the area between the whole curve and the $e$-axis, so it is the total work done for both elastic and plastic stretching.

C.explanation: This is the area between the curve beyond P and the $e$-axis, equal to $\int_{e_P}^{e_{max}} F \, de$ for the plastic stage.

D.explanation: This is the area between the curve beyond P and the $F$-axis, $\int_{F_P}^{F_{max}} e \, dF$, which is not $F$ times extension.
